qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Extensive branch network and logistics scale across North America and Europe provide distributor availability, but lack structural pricing power; margins are thin (~5.9-6.8% EBITA) and heavily exposed to copper cable pricing cycles, while multi-cycle GAAP ROIC (~5-8%) falls well below the 12% hurdle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (N, REJECT). Global electrical wholesale distributor benefiting from electrification trends, but lacks structural pricing power and fails Gate 3b. Operating profitability is constrained by thin ~6% EBITA margins, heavy sensitivity to copper commodity cycles and manufacturer rebates (Schneider, ABB, Legrand), and sub-hurdle multi-cycle GAAP ROIC of 5-8% (well below the 12% threshold). Downstream gates bypassed per waterfall.
qualitative.evidence: Reported adjusted EBITA margins of 6.8% (2023), 5.9% (2024), and 6.0% (2025). Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC historically tracks between 4.5% and 8.0%, failing the 12% quality hurdle. Gross margins are structurally exposed to copper raw material pass-through timing differences and supplier volume rebates rather than independent customer pricing power.
